frozen_claim: Показатель степенного спада alpha собственного спектра нейронных репрезентаций есть монотонная, вычислимая функция максимального ляпуновского показателя lambda_max сети; кортикальное значение alpha~1 отвечает конкретному lambda_max>0 (мягкая надкритичность), а НЕ краю хаоса (lambda_max=0) и не результату оптимизации под задачу.

observable.name: alpha_reachable_at_subcritical_lambda_via_input_geometry
observable.definition: On a tanh recurrent reservoir, jointly estimate (i) the maximal Lyapunov exponent lambda_max from a single renormalised tangent vector through the per-step Jacobian diag(1-x^2)*gW, and (ii) the power-law exponent alpha as the negative log-log slope of the sorted covariance eigenspectrum over ranks [3, N/2]. Three probes: (A) sweep gain g with a fixed low-dim input ensemble and test whether alpha(lambda_max) is monotone within that ensemble; (B) at fixed g sweep input statistics (sigma_in) and test whether alpha tracks the g-calibrated alpha(lambda_max) curve or moves independently; (C, DECISIVE) drive a SUBCRITICAL reservoir (lambda_max<0) with a power-law-covariance stimulus and test whether alpha~1 is reachable. The strong hypothesis predicts a single input-independent alpha(lambda_max) and that alpha~1 requires lambda_max>0; it is FALSIFIED if either input statistics move alpha off the curve at fixed g, or a subcritical (lambda_max<0) network reaches alpha~1 with a non-degenerate spectrum.
observable.source_ref: arXiv:2606.04426 (Bauer, Keup, Kadmon & Helias) -- seed paper that chaos in RNNs induces cortical-like power-law representation spectra; the duel tests a SEPARATE strong hypothesis (alpha as a computable monotone function of lambda_max, soft supercriticality, displacing the Stringer optimisation account) on a toy reservoir, not the paper's DMFT/cortical observable.

model.generative: tanh recurrent reservoir x_{t+1}=tanh(g*W x_t + sigma_in*Win u_t), W ~ N(0,1)/sqrt(N), N=200, T=2000, burn-in 300. Input ensembles: a fixed 3/5-channel sinusoidal set (probes A/B) and a 120-channel power-law-covariance Gaussian stimulus with per-channel scale k^{-1/2} (probe C). lambda_max via one renormalised tangent vector; alpha via log-log covariance-spectrum slope; spectral degeneracy flagged by participation ratio PR.
model.config: N=200, T=2000, burn=300; probe A g in {0.7,0.9,1.0,1.2,1.5,2.0,2.5,3.0} fixed sigma_in=0.5 din=3; probe B g=1.5 sigma_in in {0.2,0.5,1.0,2.0} din=5; probe C g in {0.3,0.5,0.8} sigma_in=0.8 power-law din=120; 6 fixed seeds per cell (A/B seeds 0..5, C seeds 100..105; power-law input drawn with rng(7)).
model.controls: participation ratio PR>8 required for an alpha to count as a non-degenerate power law; the edge-of-chaos point (lambda_max~0) included so 'alpha~1 at the edge' can be distinguished from 'alpha~1 supercritically'.

thresholds.decision_rule: The STRONG hypothesis is FALSIFIED (CON) if EITHER (B) at fixed g the input-axis points fail to track the g-calibrated alpha(lambda_max) curve (alpha varies while lambda is held or swept independently), OR (C) a subcritical network (lambda_max<0) with power-law stimulus geometry reaches alpha within +/-0.15 of 1 with PR>8. The SCOPED-sufficiency reading survives if (A) within a fixed input ensemble Spearman(lambda,alpha) <= -0.9 and alpha~1 there sits at lambda_max>0.

nulls: powerlaw_input_subcritical: a subcritical reservoir should, under the strong hypothesis, be UNABLE to reach alpha~1; reaching it falsifies necessity of supercriticality.
participation-ratio gate rejects degenerate 1-2 mode spectra where alpha is ill-defined.
failure_modes: A toy untrained reservoir cannot establish what real cortex or trained task networks do (external validity) -- the decisive limitation.
Leading-Lyapunov-only estimate; the full spectrum could matter for alpha.
alpha is a log-log slope sensitive to the [3, N/2] fit window and to spectral degeneracy; PR is used as a guard but the window is fixed.
The power-law stimulus exponent (k^{-1/2}) is chosen, not fitted to cortex; a different stimulus spectrum would shift the subcritical alpha.
Finite T=2000 and N=200 leave run-to-run spread, reported as std across 6 seeds.
accepted_evidence_criteria: Falsification of the strong hypothesis is accepted if a subcritical (lambda_max<0) power-law-input network reaches alpha within +/-0.15 of 1 at PR>8, AND/OR the input-axis test shows alpha moving off the g-calibrated alpha(lambda_max) curve at fixed g. Scoped sufficiency is accepted if the within-ensemble g-sweep gives Spearman(lambda,alpha) <= -0.9 with alpha~1 at lambda_max>0.
rejected_evidence_criteria: Degenerate-spectrum (PR<=8) fits are not admitted as alpha measurements. The strong hypothesis would have SURVIVED only if alpha had been a single input-independent function of lambda_max (input-axis points on the curve) AND alpha~1 had been unreachable at lambda_max<0 -- neither held. No real-cortex claim is admitted from this toy model regardless of outcome.
